subject: KMS choice impact on telemetry and logging — action items
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@finbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 10:52:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: KMS, telemetry and logging asks

Hi Alice / FinBank security team,

Thanks again for the call this morning — appreciate the clear list of constraints. Short recap and suggested next steps below so we have an agreed action plan: 

Recap of requirements you flagged:
- PII classification: customer SSN and payment tokens labeled as "high sensitivity"; retention capped at 90 days unless legal exception.
- Audit logging: request for per-request audit records with sampling at 100% for admin calls and configurable sampling for user-facing generation calls.
- Telemetry: must not include full prompt text for high-sensitivity flows; we can include token counts, model id, latency, and anonymized hashes.
- Residency: all production inference for this workload must run in AWS us-east-2; no cross-region replication unless encrypted and customer-authorized.
- Encryption: in-transit TLS 1.2+ required; at-rest encryption must support customer-managed keys (CMK) in their AWS KMS or HSM-backed keys.

Open technical questions (we promised to follow up with specifics):
1) For CMK options: do you require HSM-backed (CloudHSM) keys or is AWS KMS with imported key material acceptable?
2) Logging retention SLA: is 90 days a hard limit for all audit logs, or can we retain aggregated metrics longer (30–90 day window vs archived 7-year archival need)?
3) Sampling policy: confirm whether per-user sampling controls must be enforced on our side or can be handled by FinBank post-ingestion.

Proposed next steps (action owner / ETA):
- Redwood: deliver a short decision worksheet that maps implementation options (hosted CMK, BYOK with KMS Import, HSM-backed) to telemetry and logging impacts + estimated timeline — target EOD Monday 6/14. (Monica)
- FinBank: confirm HSM requirement vs KMS-import preference and clarify archival retention policy for legal holds. (Alice / Security)
- Redwood/Product: schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive to walk through network diagrams and key rotation flow (tentative Wed 6/16). Invitees: FinBank security + FinBank infra + Redwood infra/crypto. (Marissa)

Attachments: crypto-requirements-matrix.xlsx (initial mapping), redwood-kms-options.pdf (high-level options).

If anything above is incorrect or missing, flag and I will adjust.

Thanks,
Monica

--
Monica Patel
Enterprise Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@finbank.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: security@finbank.com
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: KMS, telemetry and logging asks

Monica — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- CMK preference: our default is HSM-backed keys (CloudHSM) for production workloads containing SSNs, but we can accept AWS KMS with imported key material for a staging environment. Production must be HSM-backed.
- Retention/archival: 90 days for primary audit logs is required. For legal holds we need the ability to export and archive specific events to our secure S3 vault for up to 7 years; archived exports must be encrypted under our CMK.
- Sampling: we want 100% admin-level audit capture. For user-facing generation calls, we'd like the ability to configure sampling on a per-workflow basis; Redwood should support sample rates by route or tag.

Quick Q: when you say "anonymized hashes" in telemetry, can you include the exact hash algorithm you plan to use? We need to verify it meets our reuse/reidentification risk policy.

Happy to confirm next steps — Wed 6/16 for a deep-dive works, after 1pm ET.

-Alice
Alice Nguyen
Director, Security Engineering | FinBank
alice.nguyen@finbank.com

On Fri, Jun 11, 2027 at 10:52 AM Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com> wrote:
> (call recap and action items)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@finbank.com>, security@finbank.com
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: KMS, telemetry and logging asks

Thanks Alice — adding a couple of details and a proposed deliverable structure.

Monica: I'll own the technical decision worksheet we promised. Outline below — I can convert to a one-page matrix and populate pros/cons + ops impact: 
- Option A: Redwood-hosted KMS (Redwood-managed keys) — fastest to market, limited customer control, telemetry unredacted by default but can be configured to strip prompts.
- Option B: AWS KMS with imported key material (customer-managed import) — good compromise for staging; key lifecycle partially controlled by customer; audit export supported; vault resides in customer's AWS account for imports.
- Option C: HSM-backed CMK (CloudHSM) — meets FinBank production standard, requires network peering/VPC configs and key wrapping flow; stronger attestation for key custody.

For each option we'll include: implementation effort (days), impact to logging/telemetry (what we must redact vs what can be retained), rotation story, and operational runbook (who to call for key revocation/rotation). Ben, can you add the rough E2E deployment effort and whether we need a small infra pilot for CloudHSM?

I'll have the first draft of the worksheet and a short appendix on hash algorithms (we'll recommend salted SHA-256 with keyed HMAC for non-reversible telemetry identifiers) by EOD Monday 6/14. Monica — do you want me to include a sample archival workflow for legal holds that demonstrates encrypt-then-upload to the customer's S3 bucket under their CMK?

Marissa

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@finbank.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: KMS, telemetry and logging asks

Perfect — thanks Marissa and Alice. A couple of quick confirmations: 
- Yes, include the archival workflow to customer S3 under their CMK. That will be the primary way FinBank keeps legal-hold exports.
- For telemetry hashing, Marissa's proposed HMAC-SHA256 looks appropriate; include parameters and a suggested salt/rotation cadence in the appendix so FinBank's crypto team can sign off.
- I'll lock in Wed 6/16 1:30pm ET for the deep-dive and send calendar invites to FinBank infra + security, and Redwood infra/crypto.

Links: worksheet draft and example diagrams (will be in the shared folder): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3Credwood-FB-3421

Attaching: redwood-kms-options.pdf for immediate review.

See you all next week — Monica

--
Monica Patel | Redwood Inference
